PLANET.name: Mars
src: IAU/IAG Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements
Smith, D.E. et al. (2001), MOLA areoid, J. Geophys. Res. 106(E10), 23689, doi:10.1029/2000JE001364

FEATURES.name: Olympus Mons
FEATURES.desc: The largest known volcano in the solar system: ~600 km wide, summit ≈21.3 km above the MOLA areoid (published MOLA value; 21.1 km in the embedded 4 ppd grid). Young Amazonian lava flows and a 6-km-high escarpment (Olympus Rupes). Prime science target for volcanology and astrobiology-adjacent niches.
src: IAU Gazetteer
USGS Geologic Map of Mars, SIM 3292 (Tanaka et al. 2014)
FEATURES.interesting: Tallest volcano known; huge young lava flows; aureole landslides.

FEATURES.name: Ascraeus Mons
FEATURES.desc: Northernmost of the Tharsis Montes; summit ≈18.1 km above areoid (MEGDR 4 ppd). Nested summit calderas and flank vents.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Pavonis Mons
FEATURES.desc: Middle Tharsis Montes volcano on the equator; summit ≈14.0 km (MEGDR 4 ppd). Candidate pit-crater chains (possible lava-tube skylights) on its flanks.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Arsia Mons
FEATURES.desc: Southernmost Tharsis volcano; summit ≈17.5 km (MEGDR 4 ppd). Annual repeating 'cloud spiral' (orographic lee cloud) observed by Mars Express and other orbiters.
src: IAU Gazetteer
ESA/Mars Express observations of the Arsia Mons elongated cloud (2018)

FEATURES.name: Alba Mons (Alba Patera)
FEATURES.desc: Immense low-relief shield ~1,500–2,000 km across but only ≈6.7 km high (MEGDR 4 ppd) — the largest volcano by area on Mars; extensive circumferential graben.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Elysium Mons
FEATURES.desc: Main volcano of Elysium; summit ≈13.7 km (MEGDR 4 ppd). Nearby Cerberus Fossae is the source region of the 2022 InSight marsquake S1222a.
src: IAU Gazetteer
InSight marsquake source studies (2022–2023)

FEATURES.name: Tharsis Montes (chain)
FEATURES.desc: The Ascraeus–Pavonis–Arsia chain aligned NE–SW, the backbone of the Tharsis rise — the largest volcanic province in the solar system, responsible for a large fraction of Mars' crustal thickness and volcanic loading.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Olympus Rupes
FEATURES.desc: Basal scarp of Olympus Mons, locally up to ~6–8 km high.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Uranius Tholus
FEATURES.desc: Small Tharsis volcano north of Ceraunius Tholus.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Ceraunius Tholus
FEATURES.desc: Small Tharsis volcano with a deep summit caldera and Rahe crater overflow channel.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Tharsis Tholus
FEATURES.desc: Small, deeply degraded Tharsis volcano with large caldera.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Syrtis Major Planum
FEATURES.desc: Classic dark albedo feature; a Hesperian basaltic shield plain (Hs unit) hosting Nili Patera, a site of active aeolian dune migration measured by HiRISE.
src: IAU Gazetteer
USGS Geologic Map of Mars, SIM 3292

FEATURES.name: Hellas Planitia
FEATURES.desc: The largest well-preserved impact basin on Mars (~2,300 km across); floor ≈7.1 km below the areoid locally, with the deepest MEGDR point ≈−8.1 km. Gullied massifs, possible ice-related landforms, dust storms originate here.
src: IAU Gazetteer
MEGDR 4 ppd (embedded)
FEATURES.interesting: Deepest, lowest region on Mars; highest surface pressures on the planet.

FEATURES.name: Argyre Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Large southern-hemisphere impact basin (~1,200 km); floor ≈−3.5 km (MEGDR 4 ppd) with deep southwestern sections reaching ≈−5.7 km. Outflow channels (Uzboi, Hirnan) cut its rim.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Isidis Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Ancient impact basin (~1,500 km) between Syrtis Major and Utopia; floor ≈−3.6 km (MEGDR 4 ppd).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Utopia Planitia
FEATURES.desc: The largest recognized impact basin on Mars (basin diameter ~3,200 km, topographic expression) and northern lowlands plain; Viking 2 and China's Zhurong landed here.
src: IAU Gazetteer
MOLA-based analyses of the Utopia basin (see USGS/PDS MOLA products)

FEATURES.name: Chryse Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Northern lowlands outflow-terminus plain; Viking 1 and Pathfinder landed here amid catastrophic-flood deposits.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Acidalia Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Northern plains east of Chryse; dark aeolian streaks and giant polygonal terrain.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Amazonis Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Exceptionally smooth young northern plains between Tharsis and Elysium.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Elysium Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Equatorial volcanic plains; InSight landed here (4.50°N, 135.62°E); site of Cerberus Fossae and young flood lavas (Athabasca Valles).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Arcadia Planitia
FEATURES.desc: Northern plains with widespread mid-latitude ice-consistent terrain; candidate landing region for ice-resource studies.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Vastitas Borealis
FEATURES.desc: The northern lowland terrain unit (Vastitas Borealis formations) covering much of the northern hemisphere; Phoenix landed at 68.2°N.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Planum Boreum
FEATURES.desc: North polar dome of water ice with layered deposits (NPLD); basal units hold CO₂ ice; Chasma Boreale re-entrants cut the cap.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Planum Australe
FEATURES.desc: South polar cap: residual CO₂ ice over H₂O layered deposits; MARSIS confirmed buried CO₂-ice-rich layers; subcap basins host buried glaciers.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Chasma Boreale
FEATURES.desc: Large re-entrant in the north polar cap, ~500 km long; katabatic winds sculpted its troughs.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Korolev Crater
FEATURES.desc: An ~81 km crater permanently filled with a ~1.8 km-thick ice mound (cold trap); measured floor ≈−4.6 km (MEGDR 4 ppd). ESA/Mars Express DLR stereo imaging (2018).
src: IAU Gazetteer
ESA/DLR Mars Express HRSC Korolev release (2018)

FEATURES.name: Valles Marineris
FEATURES.desc: The great equatorial canyon system: ~4,000 km long, up to ~7 km deep. Tectonic origin enhanced by collapse and erosion; interior layered deposits, sulfate signatures, landslides and possible recurring slope lineae. Floor measured ≈−5.1 km (MEGDR 4 ppd) in Coprates.
src: IAU Gazetteer
USGS Geologic Map of Mars, SIM 3292
FEATURES.interesting: Largest canyon system in the solar system; interior layered deposits record lacustrine/evaporitic histories.

FEATURES.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
FEATURES.desc: Intersecting graben complex at the west end of Valles Marineris (~1,000 km across) on the Tharsis rise; pit chains, sulfates and opaline silica in boxed canyons.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Ophir Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Northern central chasma of Valles Marineris with large interior layered deposits.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Candor Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Deep central chasma; CRISM-documented kieserite-bearing layered deposits (Murchie et al. 2009).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Melas Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Deepest central chasma; proposed paleolake basin with sulfate and chloride deposits.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Coprates Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Eastern central chasma; floor ≈−5.1 km (MEGDR 4 ppd); classic landslide suites.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Eos Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Easternmost central chasma transitioning to chaos terrain.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Ganges Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Southern branch near Gangis Chasma; Orson Welles crater exposes sulfates.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Hebes Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Closed canyon basin north of Valles Marineris, ~8 km deep relief; interior mound with layered deposits.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Kasei Valles
FEATURES.desc: Largest outflow channel system, from Echus Chasma to Chryse; ~2,000 km; multiple megaflood stages (Hesperian).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Ares Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Catastrophic-flood channel into Chryse; Mars Pathfinder landed in its mouth (19.13°N, 33.22°W).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Mangala Valles
FEATURES.desc: Amazonian outflow channel system from Memnonia Fossae toward Amazonis.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Ma'adim Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Large valley network draining into Gusev crater; likely ancient fluvial system.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Mawrth Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Ancient channel region exposing one of Mars' largest phyllosilicate stratigraphies (Fe-smectite over Al-smectite). ExoMars 2028 landing candidate.
src: IAU Gazetteer
Mustard et al. (2008), J. Geophys. Res.; Carter et al. (2013)
FEATURES.interesting: Thick, ancient clay-bearing strata — a Noachian habitability record.

FEATURES.name: Nili Fossae
FEATURES.desc: Curved graben system on Syrtis Major's northwest flank; Fe/Mg-smectites, carbonates and olivine-rich units (CRISM). Mars 2020 candidate site.
src: Ehlmann, B.L. et al. (2008), carbonates at Nili Fossae, J. Geophys. Res.
Mustard et al. (2008)
FEATURES.interesting: Carbonate-bearing strata — rare preserved alteration, adjacent to Isidis basin.

FEATURES.name: Jezero Crater
FEATURES.desc: 45 km paleolake crater with a preserved fluvial delta feeding from Neretva Vallis. Perseverance landed 18 Feb 2021 (18.44°N, 77.45°E); delta carbonates and olivine-bearing units documented by CRISM (Horgan et al. 2020; Goudge et al. 2015).
src: IAU Gazetteer
Goudge et al. (2015), J. Geophys. Res. 120
Horgan, B.H. et al. (2020), Icarus 339, 113526
NASA/JPL Mars 2020 mission site
FEATURES.interesting: Deltaic carbonates — top astrobiology site; Perseverance is caching samples here.

FEATURES.name: Gale Crater
FEATURES.desc: 154 km crater with 5.5-km-high central mound (Aeolis Mons / Mount Sharp). Curiosity landed 6 Aug 2012 (4.59°S, 137.44°E); orbit-to-surface sequence shows phyllosilicates below, sulfur-bearing strata above (Fraeman et al. 2013).
src: IAU Gazetteer
Grotzinger, J.P. et al. (2014), Science 343, 1242777
Fraeman, A.A. et al. (2013), J. Geophys. Res.
FEATURES.interesting: Ancient lakebeds (Murray formation) confirm habitable environments; Curiosity still operating.

FEATURES.name: Gusev Crater
FEATURES.desc: 166 km crater; Spirit landed 4 Jan 2004 (14.57°S, 175.48°E) expecting lakebeds, found basalts — then discovered silica-rich Home Plate and carbonate outcrops (Columbia Hills).
src: IAU Gazetteer
NASA/JPL MER mission records

FEATURES.name: Meridiani Planum
FEATURES.desc: Smooth sulfate-bearing plains with gray hematite signature; Opportunity landed 25 Jan 2004 (1.95°S, 354.47°E) and drove 45.16 km until 2018 — the distance record before Perseverance.
src: IAU Gazetteer
NASA/JPL MER-B mission records

FEATURES.name: Victoria Crater
FEATURES.desc: ~730 m crater explored by Opportunity (2006–2008); exposes Meridiani layered sulfate bedrock.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Endeavour Crater
FEATURES.desc: 22 km rim crater; Opportunity's final home (Perseverance Valley); phyllosilicate-bearing rim rocks.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Cerberus Fossae
FEATURES.desc: Active fault system; source region of InSight-detected marsquakes including S1222a (Mw≈4.7, May 2022).
src: InSight Marsquake Service catalogs (2020–2023)

FEATURES.name: Medusae Fossae Formation
FEATURES.desc: Enigmatic friable equatorial deposit (~10⁶ km³) — possibly ignimbrite or ice-rich; yardangs, radar-low dielectric (SHARAD).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Aeolis Dorsa
FEATURES.desc: Dense inverted channel networks and a paleo-delta — terminal deposits of a large late-Noachian lake system.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Eridania Basin
FEATURES.desc: Chain of Noachian basins proposed to have held a giant ancient sea; Mg/Fe/Al clay signatures (Ehlmann et al. 2016).
src: Ehlmann, B.L. et al. (2016), Nature Communications

FEATURES.name: Columbus Crater
FEATURES.desc: Terra Sirenum crater with Al-phyllosilicate and sulfate stratigraphy (Wray et al. 2011) — closed-basin lake candidate.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Holden Crater
FEATURES.desc: 140 km crater with alluvial fans and layered lacustrine deposits; final MSL candidate site.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Eberswalde Crater
FEATURES.desc: Preserved fluvial delta with inverted channels; MSL candidate.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Aram Chaos
FEATURES.desc: Chaotic terrain with hematite and sulfate-bearing layered deposits — paleolake remnants.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Iani Chaos
FEATURES.desc: Chaos source of Ares Vallis; hematite-bearing plains.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Hydraotes Chaos
FEATURES.desc: Large chaos terrain between Simud and Tiu valleys.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Simud Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Outflow channel feeding Tiu Vallis toward Chryse.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Shalbatana Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Outflow channel from Xanthe Terra; possible paleolake shoreline evidence.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Uzboi Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Channel linking Argyre to Ladon basin; breached Holden rim.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Reull Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Channel system in Promethei Terra draining toward Hellas.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Dao Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Channel from Hadriaca Patera's flank into Hellas; possible hydrothermal and groundwater-fed incision.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Niger Vallis
FEATURES.desc: Tributary of Dao Vallis.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Athabasca Valles
FEATURES.desc: Youngest catastrophic flood channel from Cerberus Fossae across Elysium Planitia; some proposals of sheet-flow ice.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Granicus Valles
FEATURES.desc: Channel system near Elysium's northwest flank.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Maja Valles
FEATURES.desc: Outflow channel from Juventae Chasma to Chryse/Xanthe.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Juventae Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Closed depression hosting sulfate mounds (kieserite) — an evaporite analog for VM layered deposits.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Echus Chasma
FEATURES.desc: Source depression of Kasei Valles; ~100 km, up to 4 km deep.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Tempe Terra
FEATURES.desc: Fractured volcanic province northeast of Tharsis with small shields and graben.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Tharsis Rise
FEATURES.desc: Vast volcanic rise (~5,000 km), load of the largest known volcanic province; controls much of Mars' topography and tectonics.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Syria Planum
FEATURES.desc: High Tharsis plateau with wrinkle ridges and pit chains; Noachian volcanic center.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Solis Planum
FEATURES.desc: Lidged southern Tharsis plateau.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Sinai Planum
FEATURES.desc: Plateau west of Solis.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Thaumasia Planum
FEATURES.desc: Southern plateau bounding Valles Marineris; extensive ridge networks.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Terra Sirenum
FEATURES.desc: Southern highlands with cratered terrain, chloride deposits, and the strong crustal magnetic anomalies (MGS MAG/ER).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Terra Cimmeria
FEATURES.desc: Ancient cratered highlands; hosts strong crustal magnetization stripes.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Terra Sabaea
FEATURES.desc: Vast ancient highlands east of Syrtis.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Arabia Terra
FEATURES.desc: Enigmatic transitional terrain: degraded craters, possible explosive volcanism (paterae), hydrated silica signatures.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Xanthe Terra
FEATURES.desc: Ancient terrain between Chryse and Margaritifer with dense valley networks.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Margaritifer Terra
FEATURES.desc: Dissected highlands hosting Samara/Himera Vallis and Eos Chaos.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Promethei Terra
FEATURES.desc: Highlands east of Hellas.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Terra Meridiani
FEATURES.desc: Meridiani region; zero-longitude reference area; hematite plains.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Protonilus Mensae
FEATURES.desc: Fretted terrain with lineated valley fills — debris-covered glaciers (ice-consistent).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Deuteronilus Mensae
FEATURES.desc: Glacier-like forms and lobate debris aprons; SHARAD-detected ice.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Nilosyrtis Mensae
FEATURES.desc: Fretted terrain boundary between highlands and lowlands.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Lycus Sulci
FEATURES.desc: Olympus Mons aureole blocks — giant landslide/edifice-collapse terrain.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Cyane Fossae
FEATURES.desc: Radial graben near Alba Mons.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Cerberus Plains
FEATURES.desc: Young lava plains (~Amazonian) adjacent to Cerberus Fossae.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Arabia Terra paterae
FEATURES.desc: Proposed field of ancient explosive volcanoes in Arabia Terra (Michalski & Bleacher 2013).
src: Michalski, J.R. & Bleacher, J.E. (2013), Nature 502

FEATURES.name: Tooting Crater
FEATURES.desc: Very young rayed multi-layer-ejecta crater (~28 km) with pristine ejecta.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Zunil Crater
FEATURES.desc: Pristine rayed crater with dense secondary fields — a stratigraphic age marker.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Hargraves Crater
FEATURES.desc: Olivine-enriched crater unit near Nili Fossae.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Tyrrhena Patera
FEATURES.desc: Ancient, deeply eroded NE-Hellas volcano; summit ≈6.5 km (MEGDR 4 ppd).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Hadriaca Patera
FEATURES.desc: Eroded Hellas-rim patera; source of Dao Vallis.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Amphitrites Patera
FEATURES.desc: Low shield south of Hellas rim.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Malea Planum
FEATURES.desc: Hesperian pyroclastic-rich plains south of Hellas.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Dorsa Argentea
FEATURES.desc: Sinuous ridges (esker-like) in the Dorsa Argentea Formation — evidence of ancient south polar melting.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Rupes Tenuis
FEATURES.desc: Basal scarp of the north polar cap (Olympia Rupes).
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Olympia Planitia dune seas
FEATURES.desc: Crescentic dune seas ringing the north cap (Olympia Undae); gypsum-rich dunes.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Olympia Undae
FEATURES.desc: Largest northern dune field; gypsum detected by OMEGA/CRISM.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Meroe Patera
FEATURES.desc: Nili Patera's neighbor; active dune migration measured by HiRISE time-series.
src: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature — planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

FEATURES.name: Nili Patera
FEATURES.desc: Syrtis Major caldera with one of Mars' most-active dune fields; HiRISE-measured dune migration (~meters/yr).
src: HiRISE dune studies (Bridges et al. 2012, Geology)

SITES.name: Viking 1 Lander
SITES.desc: First successful Mars surface mission; Chryse Planitia. First in-situ biology experiments (labeled release positive, others negative — ambiguous).
src: NASA Viking mission records

SITES.name: Viking 2 Lander
SITES.desc: Landed in Utopia Planitia; imaged seasonal water frost.
src: NASA Viking mission records

SITES.name: Mars Pathfinder / Sojourner
SITES.desc: Ares Vallis mouth; first Mars rover (Sojourner, 10.5 kg).
src: NASA/JPL Pathfinder records

SITES.name: Spirit (MER-A)
SITES.desc: Gusev crater; 7.73 km driven; found silica-rich Home Plate and trace carbonates in Columbia Hills.
src: NASA/JPL MER-A records

SITES.name: Opportunity (MER-B)
SITES.desc: Meridiani Planum; 45.16 km over 5,111 sols — the off-world driving record until Oct 2026; hematite spherules, sulfate strata.
src: NASA/JPL MER-B records

SITES.name: Phoenix Lander
SITES.desc: North polar region (Green Valley); excavated water ice and perchlorate at 68.22°N, 125.75°W.
src: NASA Phoenix mission records

SITES.name: Curiosity (MSL)
SITES.desc: Gale crater (4.59°S, 137.44°E); >30 km driven; proven ancient habitable lake environments (Yellowknife Bay), organics, methane cycle, Mount Sharp sulfate strata.
src: NASA/JPL MSL mission records
Grotzinger et al. (2014), Science 343, 1242777

SITES.name: Perseverance (Mars 2020)
SITES.desc: Jezero crater western delta; 45.22 km driven by Sol 2006 (Oct 2026) — new off-world record (JPL, Oct 12 2026); caching samples (Mars Sample Return campaign); MOXIE made O₂ from CO₂.
src: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-sets-off-world-record-for-total-distance-driven

SITES.name: InSight Lander
SITES.desc: Elysium Planitia; first seismology on Mars (>1,300 marsquakes; largest S1222a Mw≈4.7); measured crust 20–40 km thick, liquid-core radius ~1,830 km.
src: NASA/JPL InSight mission records

SITES.name: Zhurong (Tianwen-1)
SITES.desc: Utopia Planitia southern lobe; ~1.9 km driven; radar-detected layered near-surface ice-consistent strata.
src: CNSA / Nature publications on Zhurong

SITES.name: Mars 3 Lander
SITES.desc: First soft landing attempt to transmit (~20 s of signal) during the 1971 dust storm.
src: USSR mission records; HiRISE candidate debris search

SITES.name: Beagle 2
SITES.desc: Isidis Planitia; lander located intact in HiRISE imagery in 2015 (solar arrays failed to deploy fully).
src: ESA/University of Leicester Beagle 2 recovery (2015)

SITES.name: Schiaparelli EDM
SITES.desc: ExoMars 2016 entry demonstrator; crashed at ~150 m/s near Meridiani Planum after parachute IMU saturation.
src: ESA ExoMars 2016 inquiry report
